nodes.label: bytea
nodes.rationale: Binary round-trips to a Node Buffer. Measured 102400 bytes in and out, identical. Hex text form is 2×; pg uses the binary protocol so Buffers are unaffected. Use octet_length().

nodes.label: TOAST for bytea
nodes.rationale: Above ~2 KB, attstorage x compresses and moves the value to a side table. Measured pg_column_size 1185 for a compressible 100 KB buffer. Queries that omit the column never read the blob.

nodes.label: Object storage instead of large bytea
nodes.rationale: Backups, WAL, and replicas grow with blobs; values materialise whole in memory; no range requests or signed URLs. Keep metadata and sha256 in PostgreSQL, bytes in object storage, reconcile deletes with a queue. Prefer bytea over large objects (not deleted with the row).
